rules.text: If the chart's y-axis is read as temperature in °C and the printed point labels are taken as the yearly values, then the 2005-to-2015 change is the difference between the first and last printed values; a large absolute difference across the review period is the visible basis for a 'substantial trend' reading.
rules.conditions: Assumes the printed labels are the intended data values and that the routing criterion 'magnitude of change' is evaluated as the absolute endpoint difference over 2005-2015.

rules.text: If the routing workflow requires a defined threshold for 'substantial' change, then the chart alone cannot confirm escalation unless that threshold is supplied; the visible decline can only be recorded as a support gap for the escalate option.
rules.conditions: Applies when no policy table or numeric threshold for 'substantial trend' is present in the public task.

rules.text: If the visible decline is interpreted as not meeting an unstated substantial-change bar, the same chart supports keeping the record on routine monitoring rather than escalating or archiving it.
rules.conditions: Assumes the decline is real but below whatever threshold would trigger follow-up; no threshold is printed.
